summary: AtlasBank EU-Central: cascading failover gap caused streaming stalls and billing overcount — after-action
description: Issue summary: During a region-level backend maintenance window we observed a cascading failover gap in smart-routing that resulted in prolonged streaming stalls for AtlasBank traffic in eu-central. The routing layer briefly returned 200/streaming-open but with no data frames; client SDKs retried and amplified traffic through fallback paths, which in turn triggered duplicate token accounting and a billing overcount for a six-minute window. Impact: single enterprise customer (AtlasBank) experienced ~30 minutes of degraded streaming responses and a measurable billing delta for that window. Environmental context: scheduled maintenance performed by cloud partner in eu-central; Redwood routing policy had recent canary change to 'aggressive-fallback' (deployed 2026-03-09).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate primary-region pod drain in eu-central while aggressive-fallback routing policy is enabled
2) Start a long-lived streaming completion with prefix caching enabled and 4 concurrent client streams
3) Observe streaming proxy open events (200) followed by >5s silence and client-side retries
4) Verify fallback paths receive replayed requests and billing logs show duplicate token counts
impact: Customer-facing streaming stalls for AtlasBank production traffic (approx 30m window). Billing exposure: duplicated token usage recorded for the six-minute amplification period; downstream clients saw increased latency and some request timeouts. No customer PII was exposed. SLA impact: potential SLO breach for 1 route during window.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or GPU pool contention — rejected after GPU telemetry showed nominal utilization
Routing logs show a gap where stream handshake succeeded but no body frames were emitted for a subset of connections; proxies marked connection as open and clients retried
Fallback behavior replayed full requests instead of using prefix/KV cache hints due to a mismatch between client-supplied cache-hash and server-side prefix mapping after the cross-region shift
A recently deployed change (PR #7298) introduced an optimization that short-circuits prefix validation during fast-failover; under concurrent drain this allowed duplicate full-request routing
Billing system counted tokens at the serving endpoint (pre-dedup) and again on replayed fallback endpoints; dedup protections relied on request fingerprint that changed when prefix mapping diverged
resolution: Rolled back the aggressive-fallback canary and deployed a hotfix that reintroduces strict prefix-hash validation in the routing proxy (PR #7312). Manually issued billing credit to AtlasBank for the duplicated window. Enabled additional telemetry for prefix-hash mismatch alerts and added a temporary routing rule to isolate AtlasBank traffic during partner maintenance windows.
postincident_actions: 1) Engineering: revert/patch landed (PR #7312) and rolled to eu-central on 2026-03-11
2) SRE: add an alert for 'prefix-hash divergence' with a 20s evaluation window
3) Product: update routing policy rollout checklist to require maintenance-window blackout for aggressive-fallback changes
4) Billing: automated duplicate-token detector to flag and auto-quarantine potential duplicates for manual review
5) CS: proactive outreach to AtlasBank with summary, credit issued, and invitation for technical review session
